meta.title: Twelve moves toward a leaner Dossier
meta.lede: Six small moves and six large ones, plus one decision first: reshape the current code or rebuild the core from its pieces. The theme is subtraction: fewer controls, fewer blocks, one export, one look. Pick by number.

parts.markdown:
Dossier does three things. An agent turns a prompt into a structured document. A person reads it and decides inside it. The agent reads the decisions back and acts. Everything else is weight.

The strongest use is the brainstorm loop: ask for minor and major features, skim, pick by number. 0.7 makes that loop excellent first, then carries plans, reviews, releases, and incidents on the same skeleton.

1. The static file is for reading and deciding. Editing lives in `dossier serve`.
2. One page shape, many kinds.
3. Every control is explainable in one sentence.
4. Budgets are tests, and the numbers go down.

Every idea from the June brainstorm shipped. Together they produced a reader shell that carries authoring tools, six overlapping exports, and a runtime every artifact pays for. Measured on the showcase example:

spec.label: 7 controls
spec.text: In the top bar. Four of them edit the document rather than read it.

spec.label: 11 exports
spec.text: In the Export menu, plus 14 buttons in the Export Center, for two ideas.

spec.label: 5 modals
spec.text: Shipped in every file, including read-only briefs.

spec.label: 74 KB
spec.text: Runtime JavaScript in every artifact, mostly state packets and the block editor.

spec.label: 67 KB
spec.text: CSS for all 43 blocks, skins, and theme packs, whether or not they appear.

spec.label: 28 tools
spec.text: On the MCP server over ten packet schemas. The brainstorm asked for four.

spec.label: 2 renderers
spec.text: A string renderer and a React port kept in step by hand.

parts.markdown:
Together, the twelve moves are a rebuild. The question is whether to do it inside the current tree one subtraction at a time, or to stand up a new core beside it and cut over when the examples build. Same destination; the difference is how long the code sits half-broken and what survives by accident.

A clean core rests on five concepts:

1. **Kind.** A preset: sections, facets, how the reader replies.
2. **Section.** Content parts, no state.
3. **Item.** A numbered thing in a board with size, effort, impact, dependencies, and facets.
4. **Facet.** A labeled paragraph on an item, in fixed order.
5. **Decision.** What the reader said: picked, a verdict, a note. The only state.

A release checklist is a board of gates. An incident review is a board of findings with a timeline in front. A patch review is a board of files whose facet is a diff. The concepts stay put; the kinds grow, and a kind is forty lines.

spec.label: model
spec.text: One schema for kind, meta, sections, items, facets, decisions. Old block names accepted as aliases.

spec.label: kinds
spec.text: Six presets shipped, custom kinds from a pack. Small readable files, not code.

spec.label: renderer
spec.text: One string renderer, zero runtime dependencies. React becomes a typed wrapper around its output.

spec.label: reader
spec.text: Contents, search, theme, collapse, copy, decisions, pick. Under 20 KB.

spec.label: studio
spec.text: Everything that edits, injected by serve, never in the file.

spec.label: agent
spec.text: The skill plus four MCP tools: create, render, read decisions, apply decisions.

spec.label: build-time
spec.text: Kept: highlighting, diagrams, math, diff parser, DOCX and PDF, CLI, tests, examples as fixtures.

parts.markdown: In practice: new core beside the old, port content blocks against the examples, then boards and decisions, then the reader, then serve. Cut over when every example builds through the new core. Either path is days of agent time; the rebuild spends fewer of them half-broken.

The June brainstorm gave each idea a how-it-works, an experience, a why, and an unlocks line. The front door page gave each feature fixed facets, size and effort chips, an impact meter, a summary table, and a closing pick. Merged, they are the `brainstorm` kind, and the facet vocabulary generalizes.

rows: **Agent**, what the model does with it
parts.note: This page is the merged format, rendered by Dossier from JSON.

parts.markdown: The contents column sits left and sticky. Items are separated by hairlines, not boxes. Four things on a page are objects: the stat strip, spec lists, tables, and the also-considered rows. The one saturated block is the closing pick.

spec.label: ≥ 1100px
spec.text: Two columns: 208px contents rail, content column, 1360px frame.

spec.label: 820 to 1099px
spec.text: One column. Contents become a wrapping row of chips.

spec.label: ≤ 719px
spec.text: Facet labels stack above their text. Tables scroll in their own box.

spec.label: print
spec.text: Contents and controls hidden, every item expanded, hairlines kept.

items.title: Shell reset
items.summary: The top bar drops to four things: where you are, search, theme, one export.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: Edit, Blocks, Evidence, Theme Studio, the progress bar, back-to-top, and the Export Center leave the static build and live only under `dossier serve`. The palette lists only what the page has.

facets.label: Reader
facets.markdown: Opens a document, not a workbench. Every control does something a reader wants.

facets.label: Agent
facets.markdown: Authoring is unchanged. The skill describes one action: copy for agent.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: Item 8 becomes a refactor of code already outside the artifact.

facets.label: Risk
facets.markdown: Editing inside a shared file stops working until it is opened in serve. Say so in the README.

items.title: Left table of contents
items.summary: A sticky left column with grouped, numbered entries; a chip row on narrow screens.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: Kinds declare which sections are frame, which are items, and which are the rest. Numbers come from board order. Below 1100px the list becomes chips.

facets.label: Reader
facets.markdown: Sees the shape of the document before reading it and jumps by number.

facets.label: Agent
facets.markdown: Never assigns numbers by hand.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: The new shell, and a wider measure without a cramped column.

items.title: Type and token swap
items.summary: The front door tokens become Dossier's, with the accent moved to crimson and dark tuned separately.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: Thirteen color roles plus three font stacks. Three-state theming. Web fonts are opt-in with `meta.fonts: "google"`; the system stack carries the look without them.

facets.label: Reader
facets.markdown: Light is the base, dark is retuned, and the toggle wins over the system setting.

facets.label: Agent
facets.markdown: Sets one field, `meta.theme.accent`, and nothing else.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: Item 11. With tokens this small, skins have nothing left to override.

facets.label: Risk
facets.markdown: Crimson sits close to a coral risk label, so risk moves to ochre. Blue remains the alternative accent.

items.title: Facets block
items.summary: A labeled-paragraph list in fixed order, plus size, effort, and impact rendered as chips and meters.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: Items carry `size`, `effort`, `impact`, and a `facets` array. The renderer draws the meta row, the numbered title, the one-line summary, and the facets. Risk and Note take the colored label.

facets.label: Reader
facets.markdown: Every item has the same facets in the same order, so items compare by scanning one label column.

facets.label: Agent
facets.markdown: Gets the vocabulary per kind and the rule that order never changes.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: Items 5 and 7 derive from these fields.

items.title: Summary table from the board
items.summary: The board emits its own table above the items: number, title, size, effort, impact, depends on.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: `summary: true` renders the table with a generated legend. Depends-on values are validated, so a dangling reference fails the build.

facets.label: Reader
facets.markdown: Skims one table, then jumps. The biggest reading improvement for long plans.

facets.label: Agent
facets.markdown: Never writes the table, so it cannot drift from the items.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: Item 6, and the stat strip that counts sizes automatically.

items.title: Pick by number
items.summary: The closing action copies the selection as one line an agent can act on, with JSON behind it.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: Ticks and notes anywhere on the page fill the closing block. Copy gives `1, 3, 4, 7. Notes: 3: keep blue.` or the same as JSON. This replaces the decisions, handoff, and prompt exports.

facets.label: Reader
facets.markdown: Reads, ticks, copies one line, pastes it into the thread.

facets.label: Agent
facets.markdown: Parses the line or reads the JSON through MCP. Both say the same thing.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: Item 10. One reader output means one export contract.

items.title: Kinds as presets
items.summary: A kind fixes section order, facet vocabulary, the summary table, and the closing action.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: Six kinds ship: `brainstorm`, `plan`, `review`, `release`, `incident`, `brief`. Each is a preset under forty lines. Implementation and debug fold into `plan`; integration-loop into `review`.

facets.label: Reader
facets.markdown: Every Dossier has the summary, the items, and the reply in the same places.

facets.label: Agent
facets.markdown: "Create a brainstorm dossier for X with six minor and four major features" is the whole prompt.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: Item 12, and makes the block cut in item 9 safe.

facets.label: Risk
facets.markdown: Kinds can become a hidden second catalog. Keep each preset short and readable.

items.title: Two-tier runtime
items.summary: The static file carries a reader runtime under 20 KB; everything that edits moves to serve.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: A core (contents, search, theme, collapse, copy, pick) plus per-block modules included only when the block appears. Editing, evidence, imports, Theme Studio, and CodeMirror become the studio bundle serve injects. Budgets are tests.

facets.label: Reader
facets.markdown: Files open instantly and behave the same everywhere.

facets.label: Agent
facets.markdown: Authoring is unchanged; editing round-trips target serve.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: A React wrapper that only matches the reader, and a rule that plugins ship no runtime.

facets.label: Risk
facets.markdown: The largest change. Do it after item 1 has hidden the surfaces, so the split is mechanical.

items.title: Block consolidation
items.summary: Forty-three blocks become about twenty-two by folding overlapping families, with old names kept as aliases.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: `board` absorbs four board kinds, `evidence` four evidence kinds, `diff` two, `gates` two, `log` four. Validation maps old names with a deprecation warning; 0.8 removes the aliases.

facets.label: Reader
facets.markdown: Fewer idioms to learn. A board looks like a board whatever it holds.

facets.label: Agent
facets.markdown: Chooses from a catalog that fits on one screen.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: A third of the CSS and render code goes away.

facets.label: Risk
facets.markdown: MCP tools and packet schemas name the old blocks. Do item 10 first.

items.title: One export contract
items.summary: Seven export shapes become two files: the decided model and a decisions document.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: `slug.dossier.json` is the model with decisions applied. `slug.decisions.md` is the reply, notes, and verdicts as Markdown with JSON inside. Source, state, merged, handoff, prompt, and digest go away as names.

facets.label: Reader
facets.markdown: There is the document and there is what they decided.

facets.label: Agent
facets.markdown: Reads one Markdown document to learn the decisions and one JSON file to rebuild.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: Items 8 and 9, and a CLI with far fewer flags.

facets.label: Risk
facets.markdown: Workspaces and release evidence consume the old packets. Give them the decisions document plus a compatibility reader.

items.title: One theme
items.summary: Skins, theme packs, and the in-artifact Theme Studio retire in favor of one look with one accent override.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: The skin layer and theme packs are removed. `meta.theme.accent` and `meta.fonts` are the only presentation fields. Theme Studio survives only in serve, as an accent preview.

facets.label: Reader
facets.markdown: Every Dossier looks like the same product.

facets.label: Agent
facets.markdown: Nothing to choose, nothing to get wrong.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: About 20 KB of CSS and the skins module disappear.

facets.label: Risk
facets.markdown: Console Slate was built for dense process pages. Test the implementation and incident examples in the new shell first.

items.title: Skill and starters rewrite
items.summary: The skill teaches kinds and facets instead of a block catalog, and every starter is regenerated.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: SKILL.md becomes one sentence per kind, the facet vocabulary, and the item rules. Starters for six kinds are regenerated. An MCP tool lists kinds and facets for agents that skip the skill.

facets.label: Reader
facets.markdown: Consistent documents from any agent, because the instructions are short enough to follow.

facets.label: Agent
facets.markdown: Holds the whole skill in context. The first draft is right more often.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: A README that opens with one prompt and one screenshot.

items.title: React port parity
items.summary: Keep it, but it follows items 8 and 9. Its job is to render the reader runtime and nothing more.

items.title: Workspaces and release evidence
items.summary: Untouched beyond consuming the decisions document from item 10.

items.title: Packs and plugins
items.summary: Keep, with one rule: a plugin ships markup and CSS, never runtime JavaScript.

items.title: Mermaid and Playwright optionals
items.summary: Keep as install-on-demand. Degrade-to-hint already fits.

items.title: Hosted Studio with Monaco
items.summary: Still deferred. Item 8 makes it possible later without touching the artifact.
